newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NFM sees 150,000 oz a yr from Callie.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NFM sees 150,000 oz a yr from Callie.

text.p: North Flinders Mines Ltd said its Callie Wilson Shoot in the Northern Territory was emerging as an underground mine likely to achieve a production rate of around 150,000 ounces a year from calendar 1998.
Managing director Tony Palmer said North Flinders' operations were in a significant phase of transition, from largely open cut production to a substantial underground mine.

"As a result the current exploration priority will focus on discovery and definition of supplementary oxide ore sources to utilise the capacity of the existing mill and potentially provide the opportunity for possible expansion," he said.

Palmer said in North Flinders annual report that the move to predominantly underground production would result in an increase in crushing and grinding unit costs, and would affect the company's operational cash flows.
"Reliance on underground production will be reflected by a much higher capital expenditure environment, one which is more heavily reliant on longer term forward planning," he said.

Expenditure levels in 1996/97 would remain high, with expansion capital for Callie estimated at A$13 million, sustaining capital for The Granites (NT) A$5 million, and exploration A$13 million, he said.
The report said the Dead Bullock Soak mine environs, which contains the Callie deposit, remained highly prospective for the discovery of extensions to known deposits and new deposits.
North Flinders is controlled by Normandy Mining Ltd after a takeover bid, which closes on October 4.
